title: Missiles are falling, the town is burning, and all you have is a shovel. I made a puzzle where water is your only ally
author: office-canard
selftext:
FIRE MOAT is a turn-based puzzle. Missiles hit a town and the fire starts to spread. You grab a shovel and dig. Water wells up in every hole, and fire can never cross water.



But:

\- Each shovel works only once

\- Missiles keep falling while you work

\- If the fire reaches the armory, it blows across the river

\- Lose the shovel shed, and there's nothing left you can do



So it becomes a question of what to protect and what to let go. The medical tent has to be saved. The armory you can leave, but if it goes up, things get hopeless. Count the turns, find the one route, and save everyone.



It took a long time to find. It started as burst water pipes flooding a town. Then a zombie virus. Then fire, where you burn houses first to stop the spread. None of them worked. After about ten prototypes, one finally held up: dig a moat, and stop the fire there.



Nobody dies in this game. If you fail and the fire spreads, people just run away. Until the missiles fall, country music plays from an old radio. And at the end, there are the words WAR IS OVER. I love those words.



How AI fit in:

Claude wrote all of the code, including the program that generates the stages. Measuring stages by machine turned out to be a dead end: shortest solution, number of traps, none of it predicted where people would get stuck. The only thing that did was how many times you have to dig. So we mass-produced the patterns that tended to work, and kept the stages that playtesting showed were actually hard.



The child's voice on the radio I made myself in ElevenLabs, writing acting directions before each line, and Claude timed the subtitles to it. The sound effects, music, photos, 3D models and fonts are licensed assets. Claude gathered every source and license into one credits file, and I checked each one.
